newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Treasury upbeat about 1997 budget prospects.
newsitem.headline: Italy Treasury upbeat about 1997 budget prospects.

text.p: Income from the government's 1997 main deficit-cutting package is already starting to pour in though some "structural rationalization" problems remain, Italy's Treasury Ministry said on Thursday.

In a document on the measures passed by Parliament last December in the 1997 budget, the Treasury said the objectives set out by the prime minister's centre-left government were being "substantially respected."

The European Commission forecast on Wednesday that Italy's 1997 deficit would be 3.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) -- outside the three percent ceiling set by the Maastricht Treaty to join the single European currency from its launch.
It added that if all recent budget measures were fully effective, Italy might still reach the three percent level. ((-- Rome newsroom +396 6782501))
